questions.stem: Which event CANNOT happen at the same time as: "I will buy some red shoes from my favourite shoe shop."?
options: No new cars come in blue.
I only have yellow and green pencils.
My favourite shoe shop doesn't sell red shoes.
My teacher cancelled the maths test this week.
questions.hint: Look for the statement that directly contradicts or makes the given event impossible.

keyPoints.text: CANNOT happen at the same time
keyPoints.note: Mutually exclusive events cannot both be true together.

steps.explain: Read the given event carefully and identify what must be true for it to happen.
If your favourite shoe shop does not sell red shoes, it is impossible to buy red shoes there.
Verify that the other three statements talk about unrelated situations and do not prevent the given event.
Therefore, "My favourite shoe shop doesn't sell red shoes." cannot happen at the same time.
steps.work: \(\text{Answer: My favourite shoe shop doesn't sell red shoes.}\)

questions.stem: There are \(5\) coloured marbles in a bag: \(3\) red ones, \(1\) green one, and \(1\) blue one. Abby takes a blue marble out of the bag (and does not put it back). What CANNOT happen next?
options: Ben takes out a blue marble.
Ben takes out a red marble.
Ben takes out a green marble.
Ben takes out either a red or a green marble.
questions.hint: Count how many blue marbles are LEFT in the bag after Abby takes the only blue marble out!

keyPoints.text: blue marble out of the bag
keyPoints.note: There was only 1 blue marble to begin with, so 0 blue marbles remain.
This is a dependent event: removing a marble changes what is left.

steps.explain: List the marbles in the bag at the start: \(3\) red, \(1\) green, and \(1\) blue (\(5\) total).
Subtract the \(1\) blue marble that Abby removes from the bag.
List what remains in the bag for Ben: \(3\) red and \(1\) green (\(4\) marbles). Ben can still draw red or green, but NOT blue.
Therefore, "Ben takes out a blue marble" cannot happen next.
steps.work: \(\text{Answer: Ben takes out a blue marble.}\)

I pack one red and one black pair of shoes.
I pack one white and one red pair of shoes.
questions.hint: Check the three colours of shoes you actually own (black, white, red). Which option mentions a colour you do NOT own?

keyPoints.text: one black pair, one white pair, and one red pair
keyPoints.note: You can only pack colours from this exact set.
Look for a colour that is not among the three pairs you own.

steps.explain: List the exact three pairs of shoes owned: black, white, and red.
List all possible ways to pack 2 of the 3 pairs: (black + white), (black + red), or (white + red).
Notice that pink is NOT one of the colours owned, so packing a pink pair is impossible.
Therefore, "I pack one pink and one black pair of shoes" cannot happen.
steps.work: \(\text{Answer: I pack one pink and one black pair of shoes.}\)
